dimensions.assessment: Affects all civil and military aircraft operators, commercial airlines, air traffic controllers, and federal agencies operating aircraft in U.S. airspace.
dimensions.evidence: require any person operating an aircraft... to be equipped with and operating with ADS-B In equipment

dimensions.assessment: Imposes major new equipment mandates, strict narrowing of government flight exceptions, broad interagency safety reviews, and annual inspector general oversight audits.
dimensions.evidence: Beginning on the date of enactment of this section, in applying section 91.225(f)(1)... the term `sensitive government mission' shall be narrowly construed

dimensions.assessment: Requires federal agencies, the FAA, and private aircraft operators to incur costs for equipment retrofits, compliance reporting, and administrative reviews, though exact total costs are not specified.
Imposes new regulatory mandates, creates multiple new offices, repeals previous statutory exemptions, and requires rulemaking, memorandums of understanding, and repeated congressional reporting.
dimensions.evidence: the Administrator shall establish or designate an office within the FAA as the `Office of FAA-DOD Coordination'

dimensions.assessment: Institutes permanent regulatory changes, equipment standards, ongoing periodic reporting, and permanent oversight structures.

missing_information: Specific cost estimates for purchasing and installing ADS-B In equipment across the affected civilian and military aircraft fleets.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill significantly reforms aviation safety by mandating ADS-B In equipment for aircraft, restricting exceptions to ADS-B Out requirements for sensitive government missions, ordering numerous audits by inspectors general, and establishing safety reviews of airspace and military-civilian coordination offices.

card.summary: The Rotorcraft Operations Transparency and Oversight Reform Act (ROTOR Act) addresses aviation safety by requiring aircraft to use ADS-B In equipment, narrowing exceptions for sensitive government missions regarding ADS-B Out equipment, repealing certain military helicopter exemptions, mandating various audits and safety reviews, and establishing information-sharing agreements between the FAA and military departments.
card.title: ROTOR Act

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The ROTOR Act aims to improve aviation safety by expanding aircraft tracking and communication rules, tightening exceptions for government aircraft, and increasing oversight and coordination between the Federal Aviation Administration and military agencies.

affected_groups.effect: Must equip affected aircraft with ADS-B In technology by the end of 2031 and adhere to stricter reporting and limits for government mission exemptions.
Must submit quarterly reports and attestations to the FAA when utilizing sensitive government mission exceptions to ADS-B Out rules.
affected_groups.group: Federal, State, Local, and Tribal Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Subject to repealed exemptions, new safety information-sharing memorandums of understanding, and specific audits regarding military aircraft operations in national airspace.
affected_groups.group: Department of Defense and Military Branches

affected_groups.effect: Required to establish new coordination offices, conduct extensive airport safety reviews, issue rulemaking for ADS-B In and separation standards, and update controller training.

key_provisions: Requires all aircraft operating where ADS-B Out is required to also be equipped with and operating ADS-B In equipment by December 31, 2031.
Narrows the definition of 'sensitive government missions' that can be excepted from ADS-B Out rules, specifically excluding training, proficiency flights, and flights by officials below Cabinet rank.
Mandates that the Government Accountability Office review ADS-B Out exceptions, and requires annual audits by the Department of Transportation Inspector General.
Establishes an Office of FAA-DOD Coordination to review airspace usage, safety, and flight operations around major commercial airports.
Requires the Army Inspector General to audit Army aviation coordination with the FAA, pilot training, and ADS-B Out usage.
missing_information: Exact cost estimates for implementing ADS-B In equipment across the entire civil and government aircraft fleet.
Specific financial appropriations or funding allocations tied to the mandated audits, office creations, and safety reviews.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The ROTOR Act aims to improve aviation safety by expanding aircraft tracking and communication rules, tightening exceptions for government aircraft, and increasing oversight and coordination between the Federal Aviation Administration and military agencies.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping shift in national airspace oversight by forcing universal adoption of cockpit traffic awareness technology, closing reporting loopholes for government and military flights, and mandating comprehensive safety reviews of mixed civil and military traffic around major U.S. airports.
